cells.content: 伊爾德（正黃旗滿洲。初積軍功，屢加至二等昂邦章京，順治七年三月恩詔准世襲罔替，五月以軍功加為一等。九年正月恩詔超封三等侯，緣事降一等伯，又以恩詔由一等伯加一拖沙喇哈番，緣事革。四年九月以軍功復爵，尋晉一等侯，又一拖沙喇哈番，今漢文改為一等侯，又雲一騎衛。卒，諡庭敏。）

translations.literal: Irgen (of the Plain Yellow Banner, Manchu section. At first he accumulated military merit and was repeatedly promoted to second-rank angbang janggin. In the third month of the seventh year of Shunzhi a grace edict granted perpetual hereditary succession; in the fifth month he was promoted to the first rank for military merit. In the first month of the ninth year a grace edict conferred out of turn the rank of third-class marquis; because of an incident he was reduced to first-class earl; again by grace edict he was raised from first-class earl with the addition of one tusaha; because of an incident he was stripped of rank. In the ninth month of the fourth year he was restored to his title for military merit; soon promoted to first-class marquis, with another tusaha; in present Chinese usage recorded as first-class marquis, with one imperial bodyguard. Died; posthumous name Tingmin.)
translations.idiomatic: Irgen (Plain Yellow Banner Manchu. He first built up a record of military merit and was repeatedly advanced to second-rank angbang janggin. In the third month of Shunzhi 7 a grace edict made his line perpetually hereditary; in the fifth month military merit raised him to the first rank. In the first month of Shunzhi 9 another grace edict promoted him out of turn to third-class marquis; after an incident he was demoted to first-class earl, then raised again by grace edict from first-class earl with an added tusaha, and later stripped for cause. In the ninth month of year 4 he regained his title for military merit, was soon advanced to first-class marquis with a second tusaha, and is now entered in Chinese as first-class marquis with one imperial bodyguard. He died and was given the posthumous name Tingmin.)

translations.literal: Ma Degong (of the Bordered Yellow Banner, Chinese Banners. In the second month of the thirteenth year of Shunzhi, for coming over to the side [of the Qing] and for military merit, was repeatedly promoted to first-class jingqi niha. In the fifth month of the eighteenth year was promoted out of turn to third-class marquis. In the tenth month of the second year of Kangxi died in battle campaigning against Fujian sea rebels. In the first month of the fourth year was posthumously raised to first-class marquis, posthumous name Xiangwu. In the fourteenth year of Qianlong was granted posthumously the title first-class Marquis Shunqin, hereditary in perpetuity.)

In the tenth month of Kangxi 2 he was killed fighting Fujian pirates.
